chapter: Orchestra people and Xavier chamber concerts
title: Talk of red wine as 'blood' and Emil Bond's band rehearsal
summary: Banter over drinks leads Allen to a story of a rocking rehearsal at the Apex Apartments, a harmonica-playing junk-wagon man's wine names, and the Italian saying that wine makes blood.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I think I am of a module idea.
You had too much blood for supper tonight.

Thank you. Do you know that that's what they used to call Poet Wine? One night I was down at the Apex Apartments and, uh, that the band had a rehearsal where they rehearsed numbers like The Saints and this was Emil Bond's band and they rehearsed, uh, Our Society. And I'll never forget Emil Bond's saying, hey man, give me some more of that blood, you know, and then eat down that wine and drink that wine. Oh yeah? And that's the first time I ever felt a whole building really shot, rock, you know. It was really, it was rocking. You heard, you know, rocking and rhythm and the joint is jumping and the place is really rocking tonight. But it was, a whole floor board and everybody was there. Aye, aye. Ralston Crawford, you know Ralston? Yeah. He and I were the only outside of that. Everybody else was musicians or neighborhood people. It was really
something. Blood? That was port wine? I wonder if they call all red wine. They call all red wine?

I think all red wine probably. But I think it was port that night. And you know, a brother, the guy with one eye who plays a harmonica and drives a junk wagon around the French Quarter, we were recording him one day and he was talking about that old wine. And I told him, yeah, I want to drink wine sometimes myself. And so he says, yeah, I like that. They got all kinds of wine. They got the toque and they got the burgundy wine. At least he didn't say burgundy wine. Oh, good for him. Yeah. He says, and they got salt-trygling. He says, and then they got white-poked and they got black-poked. Well, don't mind if I do. Let's see, what were we talking about anyhow? I was going to ask you something. We were talking about blood.
Oh, no. No. Oh, blood. The Italians say that wine makes blood, you know. Well, so does the French.
Yeah. Yeah. It makes your blood strong and healthy. That's what it would be. Let's face it. It does warm you up. Yeah, it does. It's a cold night at that.
It is a cold night at that. No. And, uh... Oh, right here. Okay. You want some blood?
